_readme: Tableau Cloud content wiring. Two embedded dashboards: Value Intelligence (every customer) and Transportation Optimization & Savings (Vantage only). The KPI cards (Pulse metrics) and Premium benchmarks live inside the Value Intelligence dashboard. 'requires' lists the entitlements a customer must hold before the server will hand out the URL + token. 'width'/'height' = the dashboard's fixed size in Tableau. The portal reserves exactly that space, re-reads the real size from the Embedding API once loaded, and scales the dashboard down proportionally when the window is narrower.

valueIntelligence.title: Your Value Intelligence Dashboard
valueIntelligence.subtitle: Year-to-date value KPIs · Value Realization by Engagement · Net Business Value Over Time · Engagement Health · Value-to-Investment · Premium Industry Benchmarks

contextLinks._comment: When the customer selects a mark whose [field] equals 'value', the portal offers a jump to the linked page (only if they're entitled to it).

transportation.title: Transportation Optimization & Savings
transportation.subtitle: Realized savings, freight cost, mileage, invoice status and lane analysis behind Supply Chain Optimization

search._comment: Shown whenever the active sheet has a categorical filter on 'field' (e.g. after drilling into Invoice & Shipment Details). Matches are applied as that filter's values.
search.label: Invoice number

invoiceDetails.title: Invoice & Shipment Details
invoiceDetails.subtitle: The invoice and shipment records behind the summary

drilldown._comment: Optional portal-level drill-down. Only active when views.invoiceDetails.url is set: selecting a mark on sourceWorksheet opens Invoice & Shipment Details filtered to that value. Leave invoiceDetails.url empty if the workbook handles drill-down with its own actions.

agent._comment: Agent = Tableau Pulse Insight Brief. Scope = ONLY the Pulse metrics the signed-in user follows in Tableau, limited to these data sources (by name) and their portal entitlements ('requires'). Row-level security on the published data source scopes each metric to the user's rows. 'view' is the dashboard (views key) built on each data source — used for 'Open dashboard' actions.

library._comment: Report library: every view the user can open in this project, limited to these workbooks and their portal entitlements.

attention._comment: Asked of Tableau Pulse (Insight Brief) over the user's followed metrics; the answer is Pulse's. A brief takes ~20–60 s, so the server pre-builds every user's answer at startup and refreshes it every ~80% of cacheMinutes ('prewarm', 'prewarmConcurrency' at a time), also starts one at sign-in, caches in memory + data/attention-cache.json, and serves the last answer immediately while refreshing. Shorter-answer wordings were faster but made Pulse skip the metrics that actually moved.
attention.question: Which of my metrics need attention right now, and why?

scorecard._comment: Engagement scorecard built from this worksheet's summary data in the Value Intelligence dashboard.

links._comment: Signed share links (with filters) and QR codes.

authoring._comment: Build-your-own report: new workbook from a published data source (embedded web authoring).

feeds._comment: Refreshable, row-level-secured CSV feeds (VizQL Data Service as the signed-in user). Requires the user's API Access capability on the data source.

benchmarks._comment: Premium Industry Benchmarks. 'cover' blurs the benchmarks tile inside the Value Intelligence dashboard for clients without the 'benchmarks' entitlement (demo upsell — the real enforcement is the server-gated /benchmarks page). The /benchmarks page is a custom (headless) d3 view built from these fields of the published data source, queried with VizQL Data Service as the user (row-level security applies).

goals._comment: Premium: clients create their OWN Tableau Pulse metric with a goal — the portal creates a brand-new Pulse metric definition on this data source (POST /api/-/pulse/definitions) from the field below, then the client's metric on it (metrics:getOrCreate, filtered to their client + optional engagement), sets the goal (PATCH metric goals) and follows it (POST subscriptions). No dependency on existing Pulse content. 'field' / 'timeField' are data source field captions (resolved to field names with VizQL Data Service read-metadata); a measure is offered only if the data source has it.

crm._comment: Apex's Salesforce org. Upgrades are attributed to this Campaign (Opportunity.CampaignId) — the announcement that the partner portal now has conversational analytics and anonymized benchmarks.
crm.campaign: Partner portal update: conversational analytics + anonymized benchmarks

baseline._comment: Demo reset (Presenter → Reset demo) restores this: only these portal-upgrade Opportunities exist, client tiers as in tenants.json, no Premium seats, campaign responders = respondedUsers (everyone else who responded during a demo → Clicked).
